title: What does Norfolk's Zoning Ordinance say about opening a restaurant in a Ghent building?
summary: General rules from the City's official Zoning Ordinance: when a restaurant needs a Conditional Use Permit (alcohol, late hours, under 80% seating, entertainment), who decides it, the Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior changes in the Ghent historic districts. It does not say which district a given address is in, whether a restaurant is allowed there (the use table differs by district), or what applies to converting a carriage house; those need the zoning map and a zoning determination for the address.

findings.claim: A restaurant needs a Conditional Use Permit when it sells alcohol, unless it is always closed between 5:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. the next morning. (The whole list has one exception: establishments inside the Norfolk International Airport terminal complex.)

source.title: City of Norfolk Zoning Ordinance (official approved PDF, adopted January 23, 2018, updated October 13, 2026)

findings.quote: When alcoholic beverages are sold, except for establishments that are always closed between 5:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. the following morning.

findings.claim: In the Coastal, Suburban or Traditional character districts, a restaurant needs a Conditional Use Permit to operate between 11:00 p.m. and 2:00 a.m. (The whole list has one exception: establishments inside the Norfolk International Airport terminal complex.)

findings.claim: A restaurant also needs a Conditional Use Permit where seats will not be provided for at least 80 percent of patrons, or when entertainment is provided. (The whole list has one exception: establishments inside the Norfolk International Airport terminal complex.)

what_would_help.text: If the restaurant will serve alcohol, plan for a Conditional Use Permit and its public hearing before opening.
Before changing the building's exterior, apply for a Certificate of Appropriateness.

pending: Which Ghent district (HC-G1, HC-G2, HC-G3 or a commercial district) a given address is in: check the City's zoning map or ask for a zoning determination.

Whether a restaurant is allowed in that district: Table 3.6.11 (Historic and Cultural Conservation districts) shows restaurant as permitted-or-conditional (P/C) in HC-G3 and not permitted in HC-G1 or HC-G2 by the page image; a column-in-a-table cell can't be quoted exactly, so it is not a finding yet.

Rules for converting a carriage house to a commercial use: not found in the ordinance sections read. Its carriage-house provisions found so far apply to the R-C (Ocean View) district and to flood-plain definitions.
